Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=f(x)$ plotted above?

- It has a point discontinuity at $x=-2.$
- It has a jump discontinuity at $x=-2.$
- It is continuous at $x=-2.$
worked_solution:
The function has a jump discontinuity at $x=-2.$ Checking our conditions, we see that

- $f(-2)=2$ exists, $\,\,✓$

- ${lim}_{x\to -2}f(x)$ does not exist $\,\,\times $

So the second condition failed. It failed because the left and right-sided limits are not equal:

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}f(x)=1,\,\,{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}f(x)=2.
$$

These limits both exist and are finite, yet they are not equal. Therefore, the discontinuity at $x=-2$ is a jump discontinuity.

Consequently, II is true, and I and III are false.
